title: The Professor
summary: Simon Judeau, otherwise known as the Professor, was the cruel and devious founder of the Organization and one of the most powerful Seekers to walk the earth. The Professor was motivated by the desire to heal himself of a curse in conjunction to his past with Metz, Dante Vale, and father of Lok Lambert, the famous and legendary Seeker, Eathon Lambert. The Professor's signature Titan was Araknos, the Legendary Titan of the Mind.

sections.heading: History
sections.text:
Image caption: Simon starts an army

In the 1950's, when Simon Judeau was a teenager, he was a member of the Huntik Foundation and the mentor of a young Eathon Lambert. The young Judeau worked along with Metz and Eathon to fulfill many missions and to discover several Titans; within the group, Judeau served as the brains, Metz as the muscle, and Eathon as the intuition. [The Secret of Two Generations] At one point in their travels, Simon saved Metz' life at the Temple of Tecobai during an attack from the Ecuadorian natives, by holding out his Caliban Amulet to stop him falling into a river of lava. [The Divine Comedy]

Upon discovering the location of the Legendary Titan of Mind, Araknos after a year's search, Simon entered the temple and put on the Ring against his team's advice and against the warning inscription. Instantly, Simon was cursed and had to be hospitalized for several years because the effects of the curse were beyond the abilities of Huntik Foundation magic and medicine. During this time in 1958, Eathan remained a loyal friend and was by his side everyday. When Simon was well enough to walk again, he escaped and left his Titan, Dendras, behind so that Eathon could bond with it. [The Divine Comedy] Eventually Simon made a deal with Araknos that would allow him to live on for sometime until he found a cure for his ailment, without informing anyone Simon vanished.

Simon eventually started the Organization in 1959 using the mind control abilities of Araknos. Judeau also falsified the history of the Organization, so as to make it seem as if the Organization had existed for years when in reality it was a relatively new company. While beginning the Organization, Simon attempted to gain the help of Eathon but he rejected his offer. With the creation of the Organization, Judeau donned the alias of the Professor. [The Secret of Two Generations]

Image caption: The Professor reveals the truth about his curse to the Huntik team

After discovering that Eathon had found the resting place of the Amulet of Will, Simon hunted him down with five of his best operatives. Eathon managed to escape by faking his death, jumping off of a waterfall in Peru and using the power of the Nexus beneath the waterfall to escape to Huntik, the Spirit World. [Doorway to Huntik]

After Eathon's disappearance, the Professor sought after Eathon Lambert's journal, which held clues which would lead to the Amulet of Will and the other two Legendary Titans. [A Seeker is Born] Though two Huntik Foundation members, Dante Vale and Lok Lambert, managed to uncover and bond to Behemoth and Tao, respectively, the Professor used his wiles to claim them as his own. [The Divine Comedy].

Image caption: The Professor is dragged into the Spirit World by Araknos

The Professor was then confronted by the Huntik team in his castle. Though the Professor managed to invoke the Legendary Titan of Immortality, Overlos, Dante used the power of Archwarder to disrupt the Professor's control of Overlos so that Lok could use Dendras' power to control Overlos and to command him to open a portal and take the Legendary Titans back to the Spirit World of Huntik. Defeated, the Professor found himself caught by the webbing of Araknos and was also taken into Huntik by Araknos' web after a failed attempt to save him by Lok Lambert and Dante Vale. Like Eathon, the Professor currently resides in Huntik. [The Mission]

sections.heading: Personality
sections.wikitext:
[[File:S1E25_Simon.png|200px|thumb|Simon saves his friend Metz' life]]Simon Judeau originally was an honorable Seeker who cared greatly for his friends, [[Eathon Lambert]] and [[Metz]]. Among the group, Simon was the most intelligent but was also more brazen than the others, disregarding an ancient warning inscription at the resting place of the [[Ring]] of [[Araknos]].

However, upon being [[Curse of the Legendary Titans|cursed]] by the Ring, Simon removed all traces of his former self, becoming cruel, evil, and devious. The ultimate dominator, the Professor now lived to control. He was capable of being sly and manipulative, but rarely had to resort to such actions. Normally, the absolute fear he inspired was enough. The Professor had no ethics, and would do anything to expand [[the Organization]] and his power base. He was also the type who liked to manage every facet of the Organization himself and to make every decision personally. If any of his underlings failed him, he would not hesitate to have them removed. The Professor wanted to use the [[Amulet of Will]] to gain immortality and to cure his curse. He was thoroughly selfish and may have also been driven insane thanks to the curse.

sections.heading: Abilities
sections.wikitext:
[[File:S1E24_Professor_Araknos.png|thumb|200px|The Professor and [[Araknos]]]]
The Professor was bound to the Legendary Titan [[Araknos]], a devastatingly powerful Titan capable of mind control to the point of being able to completely rebuild someone's personality. The Professor was one of the most powerful Seekers in the world: he was also very strong willed, as he could invoke and control four [[Legendary Titans]], [[Dominator]] and [[Nordrake]] all at the same time, without getting exhausted, something which even [[Dante Vale]], the Huntik Foundation number one [[Seeker]], could not do. {{Source|The Mission}} {{Source|Coming of Age}}

sections.heading: Bonded Titans
sections.text:
Araknos — TV Series — banished — The Professor's signature and mind-controlling Legendary Titan, he bonded his soul to him in an attempt to cheat death; Permanently banished to the Spirit World by Lok.

Archwarder — TV Series — given away — The Professor gave its Amulet to Rassimov to stop the Huntik team, but it ultimately caused his downfall after Rassimov gave it to Dante.

Behemoth — TV Series — banished — The Professor acquired it from Dante through manipulation; permanently banished to the Spirit World by Lok.

Caliban — TV Series — Owned by Simon in his youth; given to Metz after it saved his life at the Temple of Tecobai; Dante returned it many years later, believing he was repaying an old debt and that Simon would save Metz once again.

Dendras — TV Series — taken — Once one of Simon Judeau's primary Titans, he left it for his best friend Eathon to find before he disappeared; he eventually reclaimed it and kept it in his study where it was found and taken by Lok.

Dominator — TV Series — One of the Professor's most destructive and favored Titans.

Goblin Brownie — TV Series — One of the Professor's primary Titans in his younger, adventuring days, this Titan diffused many traps for him.

Jokoul — TV Series — given away — The Professor discovered dozens of Jokoul Titans in a cavern in the Carpathian mountains, and distributed their Amulets amongst his Suits.

Nordrake — TV Series — One of Simon's original and most distinctive Titans, he was wearing its Amulet around his neck when he first met Metz.

Overlos — TV Series — banished — The Legendary Titan of Immortality, the Professor successfully invoked it following a long ritual, only for Lok to banish it to the Spirit World for eternity.

Tao — TV Series — banished — Acquired from Dante through manipulation; permanently banished to the Spirit World by Lok.

Trapfeaster — TV Series — A voracious, insectoid Titan specialized in consuming magical barriers and enemy traps.

Undergolem x2 — TV Series — given away — Given to Eathon the dog; using Araknos to implant a trap in its mind, it now summons the two Titans whenever his castle is threatened.

Redcap — TCG — One of many Redcaps distributed to his Suits, the Professor summoned his own Titan to give its power to Unnamed Titan 014.

Thresher — TCG — As a young man, Simon used Thresher on the side of good, before his curse took hold of him.

Unnamed Titan 014 — TCG — The Professor possessed a mysterious Samurai Titan that can absorb the strength of other Titans.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.wikitext:
* Simon Judeau's persona as the Professor, including making his inferiors kiss his ring, is based on the archetypal mafia boss of Marlon Brando's ''[[wikipedia:The Godfather|The Godfather]]''.
* Simon's last name, Judeau, was changed from the pronunciation of '''''joo'<nowiki/>'''-do'' in the original Italian version to ''joo-''' dā'<nowiki/>'''-yo'' in the English version.
* The Professor referred to the Casterwills as a clan of backward fools in episode 14 - "[[All Work and No Pay]]."
